body.target_estimand: \(\theta_g(\mathcal M)=\mathbb E_{\nu}[g(f^U)]\), equivalently \(\mathbb E_{\mu}[g(f)]\) on the canonical carrier

sampling_model.design: Identification is conditional on an exactly supplied observational law \(p\); an optional statistical layer consists of independent draws from \(p\) after the query, order, and alphabets are fixed.
sampling_model.units: Each observational unit reveals one factual vector \(V\in\mathcal X\); the shared exogenous response type is latent.
sampling_model.treatment: Interventions occur only inside the counterfactual query and are not randomized observations in the maintained identification problem.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed because the target is partially identified from the full observational law; known zero-mass cells receive no exogenous atom.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance function is estimated in the theorem-level kernel. If \(p\) is replaced by empirical frequencies, the compiled cell labels are fixed and the endpoints are sample means, but this standard corollary is outside the novelty claim.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The lifted linear program gives the order-only optimum, and an attaining structural causal model exists.
The \(\mathrm{SAT}^{\mathrm{lin}}_{\mathrm{counterfact}}\) problem uses inequalities over probability terms on one common domain, and Theorem~11 is fixed-parameter tractable in \(d+n\).
Input-signature satisfiability for recursive finite causal models is \(\mathsf{NP}\)-complete.
Compilation languages are ranked by succinctness and by supported polynomial-time queries and transformations.
Finite canonical structural causal models reduce arbitrary discrete counterfactual bounds to sharp polynomial programs.
Fixed structural equations are compiled into arithmetic circuits to accelerate approximate causal-EM inner-bound computation.

body.tldr: For standard finite order-compatible recursive structural causal models with arbitrary predecessor parent subsets and shared exogenous variation, sourced causal-order canonicalization permits sharp-bound optimization over a saturated all-predecessor response carrier. A deterministic normalizer extracts exactly the predecessor-only contexts retained by the query, and their complete-prefix equality partition is an exact continuation state. For the existential-support residual, in which each prefix may use its own response completion, this state is worst-case minimal: a binary selector construction realizes and pairwise separates all \(\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) partitions while the factual zero path remains outside the retained context set. Representative transitions give exact single-conjunction and joint-score compilers with exponential factors independent of alphabet cardinality, and sparse traceback attains the sharp observational cell-sum endpoints.

project_justification.gap: The closest exact order-only method proves canonical equivalence between parent-subset recursive models and complete all-predecessor response carriers, then enumerates completed response signatures before quotienting by observational and query evaluations. It does not establish predecessor normalization, complete-prefix equality as a local right congruence, or worst-case residual minimality under the correct existential-support continuation semantics.
project_justification.niche: Explicit unnested queries with few normalized retained contexts but many endogenous coordinates or large alphabets admit a smaller semantic state: later unrestricted response rows need only the equality pattern of retained-world complete prefixes. Residual equivalence compares attainable future supports and allows a different completing response system for each prefix, so it discards irrelevant numerical labels.
project_justification.fill: The project invokes the sourced canonical-carrier equivalence, proves deterministic normalization and equality-type continuation, derives complete representative transitions and explicit \(h\)- and \(r\)-dependent bounds, reconstructs sparse response systems, certifies sharp endpoints, and proves \(\rho(h)=\operatorname{Bell}(h)\). The lower bound uses \(h\) nonfactual contexts, binary subset selectors, and terminal conjunctions constant on one partition but inconsistent within a block of another. It is a state lower bound for the declared support residual, not a running-time or general decision-diagram lower bound.

body.related_work: Rossetto and Antonucci, in \emph{Partial Identification under Causal Orders by Linear Programming}, establish the order-only identified set and the equivalence permitting optimization over complete all-predecessor response signatures even when the standard recursive model has parent subsets. The present compiler takes that equivalence as its interface and tightens the query-specific construction for small \(h\); it does not redefine arbitrary recursive models as saturated. Halpern supplies finite recursive causal certificates and broad satisfiability hardness, but not a world-count continuation parameter. Ganian, Gr\"{u}ndel, and Wietheger study a different fixed-parameter satisfiability problem over inequalities on probability terms; no reduction or tightening is claimed here. Huber and coauthors compile fixed structural equations into arithmetic circuits for approximate causal-EM inner bounds, whereas this result quantifies exactly over mechanisms compatible with \(p\). Darwiche and Marquis supply general succinctness methodology but no causal residual theorem. The present \(\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) result is instead proved directly for existential feasibility supports, with independently quantified completions on the compared prefixes. Work on arbitrary graphs, fully specified mechanisms, and prescribed sparse graphs remains outside this claim.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The equality partition is insufficient when a sparse parent graph is prescribed as part of the optimization class, because a later mechanism may observe equality only on its actual parent coordinates rather than on complete prefixes. The standard order-compatible target allows parent subsets, but its sharp-bound optimization uses the sourced saturated canonical carrier; that equivalence does not license the same quotient after conditioning on a prescribed sparse graph. The residual lower bound is scoped to existential feasibility of future pins and terminal normalized conjunctions. It neither couples compared prefixes to one response table nor implies an \(h\log h\) time lower bound or a lower bound for all reduced multi-valued decision diagrams. Dense input reading, explicit unnesting, and rational bit complexity are charged; prescribed sparse graphs, independence restrictions, cycles, succinct nested syntax, and experimental-table constraints are excluded.
body.honest_scope: The sourced canonical equivalence from standard order-compatible parent-subset models to the saturated all-predecessor response carrier is used only as an interface. The normalization, continuation, representative bounds, joint truth-state compiler, sparse reconstruction, cellwise attainment, false-bit criterion, and numeric-history separation are internal results. The residual theorem proves exactly \(\rho(h)=\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) for existential continuation supports using \(h\) nonfactual retained contexts and a separate factual zero path. Its witness completions may differ between prefixes; no common numerical response-table suffix is asserted. No running-time lower bound, universal decision-diagram lower bound, prescribed-sparse-graph extension, factorized-exogenous extension, or direct nested-syntax extension is claimed.
body.interpretation: The equality partition forgets numerical prefix labels and retains exactly the cross-world coincidence information observable by a future unrestricted complete-predecessor response row. This interpretation requires existential support semantics: two prefixes are compared by whether each has some accepting completion, and those completions may be different. Requiring one concrete response table to extend both would retain numerical labels and would already split equivalent singleton partitions. The binary selector family shows that all \(\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) coincidence patterns can nevertheless affect a later causal conjunction. This is optimality for the declared online residual state, not a total-time lower bound or a claim about every compilation language.
